subject: Art & Design
title: Camera Movements: Tracking, Panning, and Dolly Shots
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Camera Movements: Tracking, Panning, and Dolly Shots.

hook.text: The Steadicam following Danny on his tricycle through the Overlook Hotel. Camera movement creates dread.

buildup.text: A pan rotates the camera. A tilt looks up or down. A dolly moves the camera physically through space.

discovery.text: Tracking shots follow a character, creating intimacy. Static shots create distance and observation.

twist.text: The 'dolly zoom' (Vertigo effect) changes focal length while moving the camera, warping perspective eerily.

climax.text: Kubrick, Scorsese, and Spielberg are masters of camera movement. Each move is a narrative choice.

punchline.text: When the camera moves, the audience feels it. Physically.

quiz.question: What is a dolly zoom (Vertigo effect)?
options: Changing focal length while moving the camera to warp perspective
Zooming in during a slow-motion shot

details.summary: Camera movement adds energy, perspective, and emotion to cinema. Tracking shots follow characters through space, pans survey environments, dolly shots create intimacy or distance, and the Steadicam enabled fluid handheld movement without shakiness, revolutionizing how films feel.
details.whyItMatters: Camera movement is what separates cinema from photography. A static camera records; a moving camera explores, reveals, and creates the sensation of being inside the story.
takeaways: Tracking shots follow characters through physical space
Dolly shots create feelings of intimacy or distance
The Steadicam revolutionized fluid camera movement

faq.question: What is the difference between a dolly and a zoom?
faq.answer: A dolly physically moves the camera toward or away from the subject, changing perspective naturally as you'd experience walking. A zoom magnifies from a fixed position, compressing space unnaturally. Audiences feel the difference instinctively — dollies feel immersive, zooms feel voyeuristic.

faq.question: What is the most famous tracking shot in cinema?
faq.answer: The Copacabana shot in 'Goodfellas' follows Henry and Karen through a restaurant's back entrance in one unbroken take. Other contenders include the opening of 'Touch of Evil,' the Dunkirk beach in 'Atonement,' and the hallway fight in 'Oldboy.' Each uses movement to create visceral experience.
